key_insight: This paper offers a concise, systematic overview of explainable AI methods tailored to protein language models, synthesizing strengths, limitations, and evaluation needs so practitioners can better interpret model outputs in biologically meaningful ways.
problem_solved: Addresses the lack of clear, domain-aware guidance on how to interpret and evaluate explanations produced by protein language models, reducing ambiguity about which XAI techniques are trustworthy or relevant for biological insight.
method: Systematic survey and taxonomy of explainability approaches applied to protein language models (e.g., attribution, probing, representation analysis, attention inspection).
Critical assessment of methods' interpretability, biological validity, and evaluation practices, identifying gaps and failure modes.
Practical recommendations and evaluation directions to standardize and improve explanation quality for downstream protein tasks.
impact: Gives AI/ML practitioners and computational biologists a clear map to select, evaluate, and improve interpretability tools for protein models, enabling more trustworthy model-guided hypotheses and safer protein design workflows.
visual_elements: Taxonomy diagram mapping XAI methods (attribution, probing, attention, embedding analysis, causal interventions) to interpretability goals.
Heatmap/table comparing methods across criteria: faithfulness, robustness, biological validity, and scalability.
Pipeline illustration: sequence → model embedding → explanation method → biological interpretation (structure/function) with example annotations.
Mini case-study graphic showing an attribution map over a protein sequence aligned to known functional sites.
paper_title: Towards the explainability of protein language models
